items.author: Madhu Guru
items.bio: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
items.summary_en:
Every AI product should be working towards abstracting model choice away from users. 

In any product, the intelligence is the underlying engine - all the user cares about is that the job gets done. 

Model picking is too much cognitive load for the user.

There have been multiple attempts to abstract model choice away from users. I think we’re finally at the point where this can work well.

It takes three things:

1/ Deep understanding of the model frontier across different weight classes for your particular use cases.

2/ Great evals for your workflows, so you know which models work best where.

3/ A team with the talent and AI-native operating model to continuously adapt as the frontier moves.

Having worked with the Lovable team, I can say they have all three.
items.summary_zh: AI 产品不该把选模型这种认知负担丢给用户，用户只关心事情有没有被干成，模型只是底层引擎。真正能把模型选择抽象掉的团队，必须懂前沿模型、有扎实评测、还能随着模型边界持续快速调整。

items.author: AI & I by Every
items.title: How a Professional Writer Writes With AI
items.summary_en:
Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:31
Hey, it's Dan Shipper, and this week I'm excited to share a very special episode of AI and Dive. In this episode, we're previewing the release of an experimental new plugin called Compound Writing, which helps you write with AI the way that we do internally. It's inspired by Kieran Klassen's Compound Engineering, and it's built by one of our staff writers, Katie Parrott. To help talk about this plugin and why Katie made it and how she uses it, Natalia Quintero is the host of this episode. She's our head of AI consulting, and she's been on the podcast a few times, and she's just an incredible interviewer.

Speaker 1 | 00:31 - 00:35
So I'm really excited for you to hear Katie and Natalia chat.

Speaker 2 | 00:49 - 01:07
Today we're talking to Katie Parrott, staff writer at Every. Katie, if if you've been following Every for a while now, will be very familiar to you. She's one of our all star writers and we're so excited to learn more about her writing process and her new plug in today.

Speaker 3 | 01:08 - 01:11
Hi Katie, how are you? I'm good. How are you?

Speaker 2 | 01:11 - 01:21
So good. I am so excited for this conversation. I am revealing myself as a Katie fangirl on on the podcast.

Speaker 3 | 01:22 - 01:23
It's a it's a mutual fandom.

Speaker 2 | 01:26 - 02:08
Thank you. Okay so Katie, almost exactly two years ago you wrote one of your most popular pieces for Every, and it was about how you had just been laid off and also maybe were in the middle of a mental health crisis, which you've written publicly about, and you decided to turn to ChatGPT as a career coach. But at the time you were also an AI skeptic, which might be crazy to think about now given some of the work that you're doing. But can you take us back to that period? What was
items.summary_zh: Every 借 Katie Parrott 的写作流程推出实验插件 Compound Writing：不是让 AI 替人写，而是把专业写作者内部那套拆解、推演、反复打磨的工作法产品化。讽刺的是，Katie 两年前还是 AI 怀疑者，是在失业和心理危机中把 ChatGPT 当职业教练，才开始真正改变态度。
